data.text: How do you primarily use the property?
data.help_text: Select the primary use of your property. Personal use refers to personal enjoyment and living. Trade or business use means it is used in a business operation. Held for investment means the property is intended to generate income but is not currently in active rental use.

data.text: Is the property generating any income through its use in trade or business?
data.help_text: Consider any rents, license fees, or other revenues generated from the property's current use in a trade or business.

data.text: Is the property classified as held for a long-term investment with the intention to generate future income?
data.help_text: This refers to properties purchased with the expectation of yielding income from an increase in capital value or future rental income.

data.text: Do you have any current expenses related to loans or maintenance that might be capitalized as carrying costs while the property is held for investment?
data.help_text: Carrying costs include interest expenses, property taxes, maintenance expenses, etc., that can be capitalized, increasing the investment basis.

data.title: No Deduction or Capitalization Available
data.summary: Property taxes cannot be deducted or capitalized as the property is used for personal purposes or does not meet criteria for trade or business or investment capitalization.
recommendations: Consult tax advisor for possible reclassification options

data.title: Deduction Available for Trade or Business Use
data.summary: When the property is actively used in trade or business and generates income, property taxes paid can be deducted in compliance with applicable U.S. tax rules.
recommendations: Ensure proper record keeping of generated income
Consult tax professional to apply deductions appropriately

data.title: Capitalization of Carrying Costs Available
data.summary: If held strictly for investment purposes with intention for future income and certain costs related to property can be capitalized, then property taxes can be considered as part of capitalization strategy.
recommendations: Document and track all eligible carrying costs
Plan capitalization strategy with a tax expert
